regions.text: たとき自魚が船に躍り入つたことと清盛が熊野へ赴く途の海上で盤が船に躍の入つたこととは機起的偶然である。

quote.translation: That a white fish leapt into the boat when King Wu of Zhou reached Mengjin and crossed the river, and that a sea bass leapt into the boat when Kiyomori was at sea on his way to Kumano, together make up a successive contingency.

regions.text: 里見弴の短篇小説に不幸な偶然といふ題のものがある。

quote.translation: Satomi Ton has a short story entitled "An Unfortunate Chance".

regions.text: 或る神経質な女が汽車の窓から硝子瓶を投げ捨てた時丁度汽車が繁華な往來の上の陸橋にさしかかつた。

quote.translation: A nervous woman throws a glass bottle out of a train window just as the train is coming onto a bridge over a busy street, and she thinks she hears a baby cry out in the street below.

regions.text: 彼女は下の往水でワッと云ふ赤子の整を聞いたやうに思つた。その後一、ニヶ月して彼女が錢湯へ行つてゐた時、天井の明りとりの窓硝子が壊れてもう少しで裸證に硝子の破片がふりかかるところであつた。

quote.translation: A month or two later, when she has gone to the public bath, the glass of the skylight in the ceiling breaks and the shards very nearly fall on her naked body.

regions.text: しで裸證に硝子の破片がふりかかるところであつた。それ以来、自分が汽車の窓から投げた硝子瓶が人に怪我

quote.translation: From then on, the story goes, her worry that the bottle she threw from the train window might have injured someone grows until she goes mad.

regions.text: それ以来、自分が汽車の窓から投げた硝子瓶が人に怪我をさせはしなかつたかといふ心配がもとになつてその女は發狂したといふ筋である。

quote.translation: That she threw a glass bottle from the train window and that the glass window in the ceiling broke together make up a successive contingency.

regions.text: 汽車の窓から硝子瓶を投げたことと天井の硝子窓が破壊したこととは機起偶然である。共他歩と現實との符合も機起偶然である。例へば或る夜、全く思ひがけない人の夢を見たその翌日その人がたづねて來たといふやうな場合は懸起的偶然にほかならない。

quote.translation: The correspondence (符合) between dream and the actual is also a successive contingency: one night we dream of someone we had never thought of at all, and the next day that person comes to visit, and this is nothing other than a successive contingency.

regions.text: しかしながら、積極的相對的偶然の意味が動相對性として遭過遯逅といふ點に存する以上は穏起性に於てよりも同時性に於て偶然の意味が到然と表は

quote.translation: Insofar as the meaning of positive relative contingency lies, as dynamic relativity, in encounter and Encounter (sōgū kaikō, 遭遇邂逅), however, the meaning of the contingent shows itself more clearly in simultaneity than in succession.
